messages:
Aisha: Heads up — we're seeing persistent GPU queue growth in us-west-2 for the live/push (streaming) tier. 90th latency for streaming tails hit 1.6s at 12:03 UTC and queued requests never fell below 400.
Mike: That's the pool with mixed dedicated and shared nodes, right? Any correlated increase in non-streaming (sync) traffic?
Aisha: Yes mixed. Sync traffic spiked too but mostly from a handful of high-concurrency customers — one account ramped 4x.
Rob: Can we surface the per-customer slot consumption? Current admission logs only show global running/queued metrics.
Jen: We have slot accounting, but the admission controller lumps streaming and sync into the same 'concurrency' bucket which is causing priority inversion.
Mike: Priority inversion = long-running streams holding slots and blocking short sync calls. We saw this pattern in CAN-41 but assumed autoscaler would smooth it.
Aisha: Autoscaler didn't react fast enough because the headroom calc uses 5m sampling. By the time it scales, queues are already long and streaming sessions keep renewing.
Rob: Two quick asks: 1) enforce a soft cap for streaming per-customer, 2) surface streaming tokens in Grafana (label: stream_slots).
Jen: For (1) we could add a streaming_shares weight to the admission policy. E.g. streaming gets weight 0.6 vs sync 1.0, then convert to effective slots. Rough sketch:

```
effective_slots = base_concurrency * weight
if streaming: weight = 0.6
if sync: weight = 1.0
```

Mike: I worry about client-level SLAs — some customers expect uninterrupted streaming. We should allow override via dedicated reservations or Dedicated pool routing.
Aisha: Agreed — fallbacks: if stream denied from shared pool, try dedicated fallback route, else return 429 with Retry-After and an X-Redwood-Reason header.
Rob: We also need a short-term mitigation: throttle long-lived idle streams (keepalive without token progress). Network stalls are chewing slots.
Mike: Add connection-level inactivity detector: if no token emitted for 30s AND no kernel progress, mark for soft-evict. That buys us headroom quickly.
Jen: Another idea: admit streaming but convert to partial-stream mode where we buffer first N tokens to reduce open file descriptors and return buffered chunk every 300ms. Less slot pressure.
Aisha: Partial-stream sounds promising; client experience might be similar for most use cases. Need QA on memory blowouts for long responses.
Rob: Ops checklist for rollout:
- implement weight-based admission in staging
- add per-customer stream_slots metric
- enable inactivity evictor behind a feature flag
- add 429 + Retry-After behavior in SDKs

Mike: I can own staging changes. Rob can own metrics + dashboards. Jen will coordinate SDK header change.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: staging/stream-adm v2 -> infra-staging (runbook link: https://wiki/internal/runbooks/streaming-admission)
Aisha: Thanks — please also add a short-term cost note: converting streams to partial-buffering reduces GPU hours because less idle kernel occupancy (estimate ~15% saving for this pool).
Rob: I'll create the Grafana panels and a short alert: stream_queue_ratio > 0.25 for 5m -> page oncall.
Mike: Rolling patch to staging now, ETA ~40m. Will post logs here after deploy.
Aisha: :thumbsup:
